name: Cronometer Gold
tagline: Log user-entered nutrition and show transparent nutrient totals without diagnosis

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Track foods, exercise, biometrics, and notes; up to 84 nutrients; charts/reports limited to a 7-day window

tiers.name: Gold
tiers.limits: Up to 95 nutrients, long-range charts/reports, fasting timer, recipe importer, and no ads

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 10 client seats included; professional dashboard and client management; 30-day trial
tiers.notes: Extra client seats cost $2.50 per client per month; an annual Pro rate was not publicly verified.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Basic plan: up to 84 tracked nutrients and a 7-day chart/report window; no published food-diary entry cap.
pricing.billingTerms: Gold monthly + annual; Pro monthly with a 30-day trial; subscriptions auto-renew and are paid in advance
pricing.hiddenCosts: Cronometer Pro includes only 10 client seats; each additional client costs $2.50/month.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Cronometer Gold, log user-entered nutrition and show transparent nutrient totals without diagnosis. The hard boundary is curated food database, barcode data, device integrations, reports, and mobile apps, plus hardware data, content, coaching, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Log user-entered nutrition, show transparent nutrient totals, and display trends without diagnosing, shaming, or enforcing restrictive goals.
requirements: optional HealthKit or Health Connect permission
whatYouLose: curated food database, barcode data, device integrations, reports, and mobile apps
large content library and social network
moatNotes: hardware data, content, coaching, and trust
ongoingBurden: sensor permissions, data quality, notifications, safety language, accessibility, sync, privacy, content review, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Cronometer Gold because people pay for polished mobile capture, trusted content, hardware integration, and coaching rather than the basic logbook. The recurring cost buys sensor permissions, data quality, notifications, safety language, accessibility, sync, privacy, content review, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: wger
priorArt.desc: Active open-source fitness and workout management application.

alternatives.name: OpenNutriTracker
alternatives.desc: Calories, macros and micronutrients stay on your phone; the app declines to become your diet coach.

facts.install: Install the iOS/Android build from the app store or F-Droid
facts.dataFormat: Diary, goals, custom foods, and measurements are stored in encrypted local Hive databases on the phone and can be exported as JSON/CSV; food searches may query the project's Supabase service and Open Food Facts.
facts.gapVsPaid: OpenNutriTracker has a smaller and less curated food database, weaker barcode and device integrations, and less mature nutrient analytics than Cronometer Gold.

alternatives.name: Food You
alternatives.desc: A local Android food diary with proper micronutrients and none of the motivational yelling.

facts.install: Install the Android app from F-Droid or the published APK
facts.dataFormat: The food diary and personal records stay in the app's local database with export/backup options; food searches can contact Open Food Facts, USDA FoodData Central, and the Swiss Food Composition Database.
facts.gapVsPaid: Food You is Android-only and cannot match Cronometer's curated food verification, broad barcode database, cross-device sync, integrations, and advanced nutrient reports.

alternatives.name: Waistline
alternatives.desc: A plain Android calorie diary that keeps its data local and its opinions to itself.

facts.install: Install the Android app from Google Play or F-Droid
facts.dataFormat: Meals, diary entries, foods, goals, and measurements live in a local on-device database with import/export; barcode and food searches can contact Open Food Facts and USDA services.
facts.gapVsPaid: Waistline is a simpler Android diary with a smaller verification and reporting layer than Cronometer's detailed micronutrients, biometrics integrations, recipes, and cross-platform history.

alternatives.name: wger
alternatives.desc: Meals, workouts and trend charts in one open-source bunker; polish is not the main feature.

facts.install: Create an account on wger.de/use the mobile app, or deploy the official Docker Compose stack
facts.dataFormat: Hosted records live in wger's service; self-hosted users keep accounts, workouts, nutrition, measurements, and exercise data in PostgreSQL plus persistent media volumes, while the mobile client maintains an offline local database and syncs.
facts.gapVsPaid: wger's nutrition module is much rougher for food lookup, barcode entry, micronutrient completeness, recipe analysis, and daily logging than Cronometer Gold.
facts.setupBlocker: None for the hosted service or mobile app; self-hosting immediately requires Docker Compose, PostgreSQL, Redis/sync services, a reverse proxy, mail, backups, and upgrades.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Gold plan and a personal general-wellbeing tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Cronometer Gold in an empty repository.
Use React Native with Expo, TypeScript, SQLite, and HealthKit or Health Connect only when explicitly enabled; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: log user-entered nutrition, show transparent nutrient totals, and display trends without diagnosing, shaming, or enforcing restrictive goals.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create optional logs for activity, sleep, mood, energy, and personal notes with editable units.
Let the user build moderate routines and rest days without weight-loss targets, punishment, or competitive pressure.
Request health-platform permissions per data type and work fully without granting them.
Show weekly patterns and consistency with neutral language and no diagnostic or body-image judgments.
Add reminders that can be muted, data export, account-free local use, and full deletion.
Include a clear statement that the app is not medical care and should not replace qualified advice.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out medical diagnosis or treatment.
Deliberately leave out extreme exercise or restrictive-eating coaching.
Deliberately leave out wearable hardware, human coaching, and a large social network.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
